primitives.name: Role Permutation Network
primitives.verbatim_quote: RolFor uses a new module we developed called Ordering Neural Networks (OrderNN) to permute the order of the players such that each player is assigned to a latent role.
primitives.assumptions: Players are ordered by latent role assignments; permutation equivariance holds under role-based relabeling.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Permutation differentiability fails under complex model backpropagation.

The core innovation lies in modeling team sports as a multi-agent system where each agent's role is latent and dynamically assigned. The RolFor framework leverages a novel Ordering Neural Network (OrderNN) to reorder players according to inferred roles, enabling a structured graph representation. This graph, processed by a Role Graph Convolutional Network (RoleGCN), facilitates trajectory forecasting by capturing role-based interactions. The mathematical duality emerges between permutation-equivariant feature learning and graph-based relational modeling. The failure mode arises from non-differentiable permutations, which hinder gradient propagation during end-to-end training. Thus, the framework balances expressive role modeling with computational tractability through learnable adjacency matrices and differentiable approximations.
